title: Assertion position map
blurb: Plots every zero-width match index for \A, ^, \z, $, and \Z with m on/off across CRLF, lone CR, U+2028, double newlines, and empty input, and verifies exact index parity with RegExp modifier desugarings.
question: Do \A, \z, and \Z match at the exact same zero-width indices as their RegExp-modifier desugarings (?-m:^), (?-m:$), and (?=(?:\r\n|\n|\r|\u2028|\u2029)?(?-m:$)) across all line-terminator sequences?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless with --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries: all three buffer escapes agreed with their modifier-group desugarings on every preset, including \Z matching at indices 4, 5, and 6 on 'a\r\nb\r\n'. Default-on Chrome 160 not yet verified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (default and --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries); not verified flag-free in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Under global matching on a string ending in CRLF, \Z matches three indices (before \r, between \r and \n, and at end of string)

friction.workaround: Anchor the preceding token directly before \Z (e.g. /end\Z/u) rather than running global zero-width replacements on /\Z/gu when CRLF endings are present.
